notices.title: Correction to historical quality guidance
paragraphs: The preserved lesson below includes outdated quality claims. Scores can be missing or Unscored; neither establishes a pass or failure. A score describes the tested cases and configuration, not the correctness of the current answer.
Additional test cases can expose failures and lower a score. Saving a test case does not itself repair an artifact. Check source values and inspect measured reruns before claiming improvement.
Chat can receive score metadata. Inspect the stored evaluation details rather than relying on an assurance. Successful execution and reviewer acceptance are separate from measured correctness.

notices.title: Correction to historical arithmetic guidance
paragraphs: Deep Analysis uses model-based analysis and synthesis. It can interpret a budget, but it is not a deterministic calculator and cannot establish that totals are correct merely by saying it checked them.

Check the source amounts and units, state the formula, and preserve a calculator result or explicitly recorded human arithmetic. Authorized code is another option where available; elevated access is not required for the separate calculation route.

Compare the actual model output with that calculation. A memo that depends on the check must wait for its result. Correct addition alone cannot resolve a missing amount, wrong input or unclear cost category.

notices.title: Correction to historical course and control guidance
paragraphs: Completing Governance alone or reading its closing lesson does not issue the credential. Every required module must satisfy its preserved course rules; saved progress and the issued certificate establish actual completion. A credential does not guarantee future outputs or grant institutional approval authority.

The course is self-paced. Earlier fixed module durations, rapid-review targets and promised time savings were not established by measured learner performance. Allow time for source checks, repairs and assessed work.

Inspect the actual saved workflow, selected inputs and step or task input settings. A chat proposal does not prove the right configuration was saved. Place a required approval before its dependent action, and inspect reviewer and timeout behavior; a written instruction alone is not a runtime pause.

Use the supported Include in deliverables download path for multiple outputs and inspect the resulting ZIP members. No future Package Builder node is promised. Inspect export contents and portability warnings, resolve permitted local dependencies after import and test the imported revision. Review status and measured validation are separate evidence.

notices.title: Current guidance on extraction settings and source checks
paragraphs: Optional fields, Allowed values and structured output control permitted absence or output shape. They do not establish that an answer is supported by the source. A required field can remain missing, an allowed category can be wrong, and an optional field can still contain an invented value. Missing evidence is not automatically No.

Two-pass extraction attempts a draft and refinement, with separately configurable models and reasoning settings. Refinement can retain or introduce an error, and refinement failure can return the first-pass draft. A completed result does not prove two successful independent checks.

Consensus starts with two attempts and can add another when their answers disagree. Agreement is consistency, not proof of truth. Calls and usage also depend on passes, field grouping and failure handling; there is no guaranteed three-call or three-times-cost rule, or guaranteed highest accuracy.

Field grouping depends on enabled chunking and its configured group size; a list exceeding 20 fields does not automatically activate it. Inspect the saved settings and compare actual results with representative sources.

Treat the original worked repair as an illustration, not an executed result or guarantee. Establish a repair by inspecting the saved revision, running that revision on the intended source and checking the new amount, period, unit and other required values. Retain unresolved evidence instead of claiming success.

notices.title: Current guidance on connected inputs and supported conclusions
paragraphs: A step receives its configured sources, which may include the preceding output, workflow documents or a selected document. Tasks normally use the step input but can have an explicit override. Inspect the saved settings and actual intermediate results rather than assuming every step sees only its predecessor or all workspace documents.

Extraction is useful when fixed fields preserve the context needed downstream; it is not required before every Prompt. More steps do not guarantee better answers. A written reviewer checkpoint does not itself pause execution; configure and test the actual approval boundary when an action must wait.

The original worked chain is illustrative, not evidence of your assigned run. Its example amount and precise reporting date are not answer keys for the assigned subaward. Check the assigned source and required budget scope. Reporting frequency alone may not establish the first due date; comparison with an institutional standard requires the actual reference rule.

Prompt, Formatter and post-process instructions can introduce unsupported claims or remove uncertainty. Check each saved result against its inputs and source. Preserve failed history and successful outputs before recovery; a canceled or lost chat reply does not undo executed work.

notices.title: Current guidance on batch coverage and targeted recovery
paragraphs: Batch mode queues one workflow execution per selected document; workers need not finish in selection order. Inspect per-document results and reconcile the actual inputs. An aggregate Completed label can coexist with failed items, and completed processing does not prove correct values.

A basic pilot is useful but one easy document does not establish accuracy across a varied collection. Inspect effective models and overrides, source-supported values and measured usage. Batch mode does not guarantee that a validation plan ran or automatically merge every output into a correct dataset.

For an unreadable scan, inspect the text actually available, repair the permitted source or ingestion and check the repaired text before a new run. Re-uploading identical poor bytes is not a guaranteed repair. Preserve successful results and the original failure, select only the justified retry input, and verify any already-executed external action before repeating it.

A batch download can omit failed or unfinished items. Inspect its actual members and retain an exception list. A small random spot check and a plausible result do not prove every output is correct; source-check the values required for the task. The thirty-proposal story is illustrative, not an executed result.

notices.title: Current guidance on generated files and release scope
paragraphs: File generation does not establish correctness or permission to share. Identify the intended recipient and data scope, inspect the actual file, and preserve unresolved content. A download-only exercise does not authorize sending files externally.

An output task receives its configured input. Data Export needs suitable tabular input for CSV; a narrative paragraph does not automatically preserve the original rows, and sibling tasks do not get different sources just because their formats differ. Inspect saved source settings, actual output format and warnings.

The original two-deliverable story is illustrative. Its publication count, delay and spending percentage are not verified answer keys. Preserve reviewed rows for the data export and supply the intended source for the narrative, then compare both actual files with the assigned report. Include in deliverables can bundle marked outputs; inspect every ZIP member rather than assuming one download contains complete, usable and authorized files.

notices.title: Current guidance on sharing receipts and imported workflows
paragraphs: A sharing request and an imported file are separate from an assessed course completion. Use the course check and completion actions to establish saved credit under your existing requirements. Examiner review remains a separate product process; it is not a routine certification grading queue.

Inspect a workflow export before sharing it: it can contain prompts, extraction definitions, text validation inputs and exporter metadata. Confirm the intended audience and data scope. Export/import does not automatically carry every source, access right, configured model or integration.

Inspect portability warnings and the imported tasks, resolve authorized local references, and test the imported revision. Keep the tested original and imported/adapted revisions distinguishable. Record actual sharing and validation evidence; successful import alone does not establish readiness or make the original score current.

notices.title: Current guidance on model evidence and training examples
paragraphs: A language model generates from learned patterns and supplied context. Fluent explanations and plausible citations are not evidence checks. Tool-enabled chat can retrieve information and perform supported actions, but the actual source, permissions and tool results must be inspected. Model generation alone is not a current search.

Structured output makes comparison easier; it does not guarantee complete, correct or identical output on every document. Preserve units, periods, conditions and missing values. A retrieved passage can be incomplete or belong to the wrong source; inspect its meaning and identity rather than treating a citation as proof.

The proposal-intake and twelve-proposal stories are illustrative. Their minutes-versus-hours and thirty-minute comparisons were not measured learner results. A platform name or institutionally managed interface does not by itself establish the permitted data route; use only configured, authorized sources and providers.

Separate proposal, creation, execution, verification and delivery. Confirmation behavior differs by operation; request proposal-only help when review must come first. A successful first document, saved artifact or generated file does not establish the whole task succeeded or authorize wider release.

notices.title: Current guidance on source readiness and first-run evidence
paragraphs: Use the assigned training document and your saved course requirements. The five-field example is not a completed run or a change to the original three-field base and five/eight-field enrichment criteria. Expected names and amounts in a lesson are not substitutes for actual extracted values and source checks.

Uploading or selecting a file does not establish that preparation succeeded or that every relevant passage is readable. Inspect the actual text and source identity. Tables, scans and conversion can lose values or meaning; repair failed preparation before relying on extraction.

An extraction template, a saved workflow, a completed operation and a verified answer are different evidence. Structured output and a reusable design do not guarantee truth on every document. Check required values, units, periods and missing support against the intended source.

Chat uses selected files, project knowledge, attached knowledge bases and public web tools according to the active context and available capabilities. Retrieval can cover only selected passages, and project context does not confine every tool to that project. Name the allowed scope, inspect proposed targets and distinguish unavailable retrieval from no matching evidence.

Preserve existing artifacts and results when a reply or operation fails. Read saved status before repeating work, re-establish missing context, and repair only the justified failure. Stopping a reply is not rollback. Reading this guidance neither runs the lab nor awards credit.

notices.title: Current guidance on process fit and review boundaries
paragraphs: The original 80/20 and 70/30 work splits, fixed step counts and implied automation savings are illustrative, not measured performance. Repetition is one consideration; source quality, review cost, exceptions and maintenance matter too. A rare complex task can still benefit from a reusable process, and a frequent simple task may need only bounded chat or extraction.

Choose a method by the evidence it must produce. Code needs checked inputs and a correct formula. A Code Execution suggestion does not make a restricted capability available; use an authorized deterministic or independently checked route when appropriate. Model-based formatting and analysis still need review.

Define allowed inputs, intended outputs, excluded actions and a stopping condition before delegating. Place the authorized reviewer before the consequential action. A process-map box or prompt instruction does not itself enforce an approval pause; end the automated portion before that action if a real pause cannot be verified.

The progress-report example is a training map, not permission to enter a sponsor portal or contact anyone. Keep preparation, institutional judgment and actual delivery distinct. Use fictional examples when a real workplace process would expose sensitive information.

notices.title: Current guidance on workflow fit and implemented approvals
paragraphs: Extract, reason and deliver is one design pattern, not a measured universal best method. A focused Prompt can read an appropriate source directly; an Extraction is useful when its fields preserve the context needed downstream. Neither shortening the input nor adding steps guarantees better results, and the original reference to teams getting better answers was not supporting performance evidence.

Inspect the saved input source for each step and any task override. Supply required reference terms as well as source facts; do not assume every earlier file or result is available automatically. Check intermediate results and preserve uncertainty through formatting.

Confirming artifact creation, confirming execution and deciding a paused workflow review are different actions. Place and test a real Approval step before any dependent consequential operation. Review timeout behavior and actual approve/reject outcomes; a written checkpoint is not a runtime pause.

Approval records a decision and requests resumption; inspect the subsequent status rather than assuming completion. Rejection does not undo earlier effects. Revising a workflow does not rewrite an earlier run, and canceling a proposed action is not the same as rejecting a review, stopping execution or rollback. Preserve existing results before any justified new run.

notices.title: Current guidance on available nodes and parallel dependencies
paragraphs: Available node types depend on the current editor, role and configuration; a fixed count in the original lesson is not a capability guarantee. Choose an operation for the task and inspect its actual output. Deep Analysis uses model analysis and synthesis, not deterministic arithmetic or independent source verification.

The original course retains its advanced-node and parallel-task requirements. An available internal Deep Analysis route avoids unnecessary external credentials; keep exact calculations independently checked. Code Execution remains restricted. Any change to those requirements must be explicit and preserve earned credit.

Tasks in one step can execute concurrently but do not automatically receive a sibling’s newly produced result. They normally share the step input unless an override is configured. An action that depends on a completed check or approval must wait for it; do not place the dependent send beside the check and assume ordering.

Inspect every task result, its labels and warnings. A sibling failure does not roll back an already completed external action. Preserve results and establish actual effects before retrying. Keep passwords and API keys out of prompts, chat, screenshots and submitted evidence.

notices.title: Current guidance on validation evidence and retesting
paragraphs: A nonempty field, valid format or repeated value does not establish source accuracy. Check the relevant source and the intended meaning of the field. Expected values and model-evaluator explanations need review; unavailable or skipped checks are not demonstrated passes.

A validation plan describes checks; saving it does not automatically validate every later execution. Source identity, source suitability and execution configuration affect what the result establishes. Validation can expose these failures without acting as an access-control or authorization boundary.

Use representative ordinary, difficult, ambiguous and missing-value cases with source-checked expectations. Keep some cases separate from prompt tuning. More checks or a high score do not establish complete coverage, and an unresolved value must not be invented merely to fill a field.

Recheck after changes to fields, sources, prompts, structure, strategy or model configuration. Preserve the original failure, saved change and new execution. Retest the failure and representative regression cases, and explain changes to the test set. Removing difficult cases is not evidence of a better workflow.

Quality history records measured conditions; its existence or an absence of alerts does not prove every current output was checked. Inspect actual run identities, available checks and relevant source evidence before relying on a result. This guidance adds no new grading requirements to your original course.

notices.title: Current controls for the original foundations lab
paragraphs: Use Library → New → New Workflow, then the Extractions task. Set Up Lab prepares the assigned sample only when its resulting status confirms readiness. Preserve the original three-field base and separate enrichment criteria.

Inspect selected, fixed and project inputs before Run. Some configurations have valid input without a manually selected document; read the current input hint. Check actual run results against the assigned source.

notices.title: Current controls for the original extraction engine lab
paragraphs: The original base requires at least 15 relevant fields; optional field-count enrichment is separate. Use precise instructions and source-supported meaning, not extra meaningless fields to satisfy a counter.

Allowed values constrains categories but does not prove a value is supported. Optional changes validation treatment, not source truth; multiple people alone do not make a field optional. Save and inspect settings, then verify an actual retest after repair.

notices.title: Current controls for the original multi step lab
paragraphs: The current task picker labels are Extractions, Prompts and Format; Format is the Formatter operation in the original three-step course. Preserve that saved three-step requirement.

Inspect each step input and task override, connect the intended results and verify intermediate output. A later step cannot be assumed to recover omitted source context, and formatting must preserve uncertainty.

notices.title: Current controls for the original batch processing lab
paragraphs: The editor labels the batch checkbox Run per document followed by the selected run count. It appears for multiple selected documents; choose the three distinct assigned samples and inspect all configured input sources before Run.

Inspect every item and its source identity. Batch Complete can include failures. Preserve successful outputs; verify the repair and use only affected inputs for a justified new run. One selected document uses a normal run; retain its relationship to the original batch failure.

module_notices.title: Current guidance on earning the credential
paragraphs: Completing Governance alone does not issue the Vandal Workflow Architect credential. Every required module must satisfy its original course rules. Use your saved course progress and issued certificate to establish actual completion; reading this module is not a completion receipt.

module_notices.title: Current guidance on course pace
paragraphs: This course is self-paced. Fixed module times in the original description were not established by measured learner performance. Allow time for reading, source checking, repairs and assessed work, and return to your saved reading place when needed.

module_notices.title: Known limitation in historical star guidance
paragraphs: The original three-star description says four task types, but this course version’s saved grading rule requires at least five task types and counts them across the learner’s workflows. The description and grading rule therefore disagree. Those historical counts do not establish one correctly executed workflow or a verified output.

Do not add unrelated tasks or unnecessary steps simply to pursue an optional star. This notice does not introduce a replacement grading rule, award stars or change required module completion. Existing requirements and earned credit remain preserved. A supported equivalent assessment still requires a separately reviewed course amendment or optional new course release.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Foundations
paragraphs: The original base requires three matching fields, while five- and eight-field enrichment are separate. Example names and amounts are teaching targets, not proof of an executed result; inspect the assigned source and actual output.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Thinking in Workflows
paragraphs: Repetition alone does not establish suitability. Include source quality, exceptions, review and maintenance costs; use a fictional or authorized example rather than exposing sensitive workplace information.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Workflow Design
paragraphs: Step separation should serve a dependency, reusable result or review boundary. Splitting by default and fixed step counts do not guarantee quality; preserve the context each operation needs.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Extraction Engine
paragraphs: The original base is 15 fields, with 20- and 25-field enrichment. Allowed values is a category constraint, not source verification. Optional affects validation treatment; multiple possible people do not by themselves justify making a field optional.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Multi-Step Workflows
paragraphs: The current picker labels are Extractions, Prompts and Format; Format is the Formatter operation in the original criteria. Inspect configured inputs and intermediate results, and preserve unsupported deadlines or obligations as unresolved.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Advanced Nodes
paragraphs: Deep Analysis uses model reasoning and is not a deterministic calculator. Verify source figures and arithmetic independently. It supplies an internal route for the original advanced-node requirement; preserve the parallel-task requirement and keep dependent operations after their prerequisites.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Validation & QA
paragraphs: Presence and numeric format do not establish the correct amount. Verify expected values against the source and inspect actual evaluation records. Saving a plan or retaining an old score does not validate every later execution.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Batch Processing
paragraphs: Use a suitable saved workflow; Process Mapping does not itself supply one. Reconcile every assigned distinct document with its own result. A terminal batch status can include failures and does not prove accurate output.

module_notices.title: Current guidance for Collaboration & Governance
paragraphs: Checked denotes examiner review, not production readiness for your use. Inspect measured validation separately. The original course retains its sharing and optional review-star rules; sharing alone does not save course completion. No new staff certification grading queue is created by this guidance.
